Ingredients
Unsalted butter: 1/2 cup (1 stick), melted
Vegetable oil: 2 tbsp
Granulated sugar: 1 cup
Brown sugar: 1/2 cup (packed)
Large eggs: 2 (at room temperature)
Vanilla extract: 2 tsp
All-purpose flour: 1/2 cup
Unsweetened cocoa powder: 1/2 cup
Salt: 1/4 tsp
Dark or semi-sweet chocolate chips: 3/4 cup
Instructions
Prep: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment paper.
Mix Wet Ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk the melted butter, oil, and sugars together vigorously for about a minute. Whisk in the eggs and vanilla until the batter becomes pale and glossy.
Fold Dry Ingredients: Sift in the flour, cocoa powder, and salt. Gently fold with a spatula just until combined—do not overmix. Gently fold in the chocolate chips.
Bake: Pour into the prepared pan and bake for 20 to 25 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the center should come out with wet, fudgy crumbs (not wet batter).
Cool: Let them cool completely in the pan so the center sets into a dense, creamy texture before slicing.
Enjoy your brownie!

@elijahongmusic in future, all you need to do is find the midi on the internet (or play some in yourself if you feel so inclined), get a sampler (I use simpler, one of ableton's default samplers), add the midi to the track and then just drag the sound file in, trim it down, switch it to 1-shot, transpose it as you wish and you're done. 

I don't believe simpler has precise pitch control, so for a better sound you can also try dragging the audio file into the grid or session view directly, using auto tune, fine pitch control or both to tune the vocal fragment and then freezing and flattening the track. 

If autotune seems like too much of a cost investment you can get a subscription license, I believe I got mine from splice.

All of this advice is for ableton and can be done using the tools available to you. Bear in mind things may be slightly different as I have not yet upgraded from 10 because I'm not paying 600 fucking euros for half-assed producer DLC
